reviewed_replacements.before: Skills are where the Rogue level pays for itself. Two wiki rules shape the whole plan. First, one level of a class “permanently raises that skill’s maximum rank to (3 + character level)” for every one of that class’s skills (Cross-class skill page), so Rogue at level 1 lets Disable Device, Open Lock, Use Magic Device, Tumble, Bluff, Diplomacy and Balance be trained to the full maximum (23 at level 20) for the rest of the life. Second, a rank still costs 2 points on any level where the skill is cross-class, and Ranger’s class skills are Concentration, Heal, Hide, Jump, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Spot and Swim (Ranger page); none of the Rogue list is on it. So the Rogue-only skills cost double on Ranger and past-life-class levels, and the plan is built around that.
reviewed_replacements.after:
Skills are where the Rogue level pays for itself. Two wiki rules shape the whole plan. First, one level of a class “permanently raises that skill’s maximum rank to (3 + character level)” for every one of that class’s skills (Cross-class skill page), so Rogue at level 1 lets Disable Device, Open Lock, Use Magic Device, Tumble, Bluff, Diplomacy and Balance be trained to the full maximum (23 at level 20) for the rest of the life. Second, each rank costs 1 skill point when the skill is a class skill of the class being advanced, or 2 points when it is cross-class and can be trained (Skill point and Class skill). A prior Rogue level raises those maximums; it does not make later levels use Rogue prices. Ranger’s class skills are Concentration, Heal, Hide, Jump, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Spot and Swim (Ranger page), so those seven Rogue skills cost 2 per rank on Ranger levels. Past-life-class levels use the class being advanced, which can make some of those skills 1-point purchases.

The cost column gives named class-skill examples, not an exhaustive list of classes or archetypes. Check the actual class being advanced, including its archetype; an unlisted class is not automatically cross-class. The 8 November source notes retain the unresolved Barbarian Balance and Dark Hunter Spot pricing limits. These price corrections do not verify the existing total budgets or change the selected ranks and priorities.
